workflow:
# Building UI with Nucleux

Nucleux (`@nucleux/react`) is a React + Tailwind design system. The `nucleux` MCP
server holds its curated page patterns and exact component contracts. Work
design-first: find the pattern, read the contracts, then write code.

## Rules

1. Inspect the project before changing files. Keep its framework, router,
   state management, business logic and file layout.
2. Look for a Nucleux pattern (`search_patterns`) before laying out any page.
   Prefer a whole pattern over assembling unrelated components.
3. Read the contract (`get_component`) before using a component. Use only the
   imports, props and variant values it lists. Never guess a Nucleux export,
   prop or variant. If it is not in the catalog, it does not exist.
4. Do not rebuild something Nucleux already ships (navigation, tables, cards,
   dialogs, sheets, form controls, empty/error states). If you must, say why
   in your summary.
5. Style with the semantic token classes (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`,
   `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, `text-destructive`…).
   No hex colors, no arbitrary color values. Use the same variant for the same
   meaning everywhere (one `cta` primary action per page, `destructive` only
   for destructive actions).
6. Every page must work from 360px wide: follow each pattern's responsive rules.
7. Accessibility is part of done: labels for every control, `aria-label` on
   icon-only buttons, visible focus, status not conveyed by color alone.
8. Every data view handles loading, empty and error (the `page-states` pattern).
9. When Nucleux has no pattern or component for a need, build it from Nucleux
   primitives (or the ShadCN equivalent the tools name), keep it on Nucleux
   tokens, and report the gap. Never present an invented component as Nucleux.
10. Nucleux is not mandatory. If the project already uses another component
    system and the user did not ask to switch, extend that system and say so.

## Workflow

**A. Inspect the project.** Find the framework (Vite, Next.js, Remix…), package
manager (lockfile), TypeScript, Tailwind version and config, router, existing
component system, and any installed `@nucleux/*` packages. If Nucleux is not set
up, call `get_setup` and follow it exactly.

**B. Analyse the request.** List the pages, the main user journeys, the key
interactions on each page, and what matters most on each screen. Ask only about
ambiguities that change the architecture; pick sensible defaults otherwise.

**C. Discover.** For each page call `search_patterns` with what the page is for,
then `get_pattern` for the best match (`app-shell` for the frame, plus one
pattern per page). Call `get_component` for every component you will use that
you have not read in this session. Use `search_components` for needs inside a
page that no pattern covers.

**D. Plan.** Write a short plan: shared layout, then each route →
pattern(s) → components → app-specific pieces you will write → states. Mark
anything Nucleux does not cover.

**E. Implement.** Build the shared shell once and wrap every route in it.
Start each page from its pattern's example, replace the sample data with the
app's data model, and keep app-specific components (a TaskCard bound to your
data) in the app, composed from Nucleux parts.

**F. Validate.** Run the project's type check, lint, tests and production build;
fix every error. Re-check each page against its pattern's responsive and
accessibility rules. If the MCP server offers `validate_design`, run it on your
plan or composition.

**G. Report.** Summarise the pages built, the patterns and components used per
page, design decisions, the checks you ran and their results, anything you built
custom and why, and the gaps or open issues.

patterns.name: Application shell
patterns.summary: Persistent left navigation, top bar with search and account, and a mobile navigation sheet around the page content.
patterns.description: The frame every page of a multi-page web app renders inside. On large screens a NavPanel column holds the primary navigation; below the lg breakpoint it is replaced by a menu button in the GlobalNav that opens the same links in a left Sheet. Build it once and wrap every route in it.
whenToUse: The app has three or more top-level sections the user switches between.
Pages share global search, notifications or an account menu.
whenNotToUse: Single-page tools or landing pages with no section navigation.
Chat-first agent UIs: use the agent-chat example (get_example) instead.
The project already has a working shell: reuse it and only swap inner components.

children.role: Desktop navigation column, hidden below lg
One link per section; active marks the current route
left slot: opens the navigation Sheet, visible below lg
center slot: global search, hidden below sm
Scrollable page content; each route renders here
Same NavSection/NavItem list as the desktop column

layout: Root is a full-height flex row; only <main> scrolls (min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto).
NavPanel is a fixed 16rem (w-64) column; the content column must be min-w-0 so tables can scroll inside it.
Render one nav list component and reuse it in both NavPanel and Sheet so links never diverge.
Pages inside <main> own their padding and max width (see list-page, dashboard-overview).
responsive: lg and up: NavPanel visible (hidden lg:flex); menu IconButton hidden (lg:hidden).
Below lg: NavPanel hidden; IconButton opens the Sheet; close the Sheet after navigating.
Below sm: hide the center SearchInput (containerClassName="hidden sm:flex") or move search into the page.
GlobalNav default horizontal padding is px-6; pass className="px-4 sm:px-6" on narrow screens.
accessibility: Give the navigation an accessible name (aria-label="Primary") in both places it renders.
IconButton requires aria-label ("Open navigation", "Notifications").
NavItem sets aria-current="page" when active; drive active from the router, not local state.
Sheet is role=dialog aria-modal with its title wired to aria-labelledby; always render SheetTitle.
patterns.routing: NavItem renders an <a>. Keep href for real URLs and call preventDefault + your router's navigate in onClick (React Router, TanStack Router); in Next.js wrap with next/link's legacyBehavior or call router.push.
antiPatterns: Hand-rolling a sidebar <aside> with custom link styles instead of NavPanel/NavItem.
Rendering the shell inside each page instead of once around the routes.
Two separately maintained link lists for desktop and mobile.
Hiding navigation on mobile with no way to reach it.

npm.name: lucide-react
npm.reason: Icons in the example. Any icon set works.

patterns.name: Dashboard overview
patterns.summary: KPI metric cards, a progress panel and a recent-activity table in a responsive card grid.
patterns.description: The home page of a SaaS or admin app: what matters right now at a glance. Every region is a CardContainer so regions can be added, removed or reordered without changing the grid.
whenToUse: Users need a summary of several metrics and recent changes before drilling in.
whenNotToUse: Charting-heavy analytics: Nucleux ships @nucleux/chart (ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartLegend over Recharts) — check get_component chart and add chart cards to this grid rather than a separate layout.
A page with one dominant task (use list-page or a form).

children.role: MetricCard: label, large tabular value, change line

layout: 4 KPIs maximum in the top row; more belong on an analytics page.
Use tabular-nums for metric values so digits align.
Every region is a card with a CardTitle; no free-floating content between cards.
responsive: Detail grid: stacked below lg, lg:grid-cols-3 with the table spanning 2.
Hide low-priority table columns below sm (hidden sm:table-cell) and wrap tables in overflow-x-auto.
accessibility: CardTitle renders an <h3>. Directly under the page's <h1> (PageHeader) pass aria-level={2} so the heading order does not skip a level.
Label the KPI section (aria-label="Key metrics").
Decorative metric icons get aria-hidden.
Every Progress needs an aria-label naming what it measures.
patterns.states: While data loads render Skeleton blocks in each card at the same size; on failure show ErrorState inside the affected card only, so the rest of the dashboard stays usable.
antiPatterns: Raw hex colors for trend arrows: use text-success / text-destructive tokens.
Hand-built progress bars with divs instead of Progress.

patterns.name: Collection list page with search, filter and pagination
patterns.summary: Page header with the primary create action, a search + filter toolbar, and a sortable paginated DataTable.
patterns.description: The standard page for browsing a collection of records (projects, tasks, users, orders, bookings). Filtering runs before the table, so DataTable's built-in sorting and pagination always apply to the filtered rows.
whenToUse: Users scan, search, filter or sort many records of the same shape.
whenNotToUse: Fewer than ~5 items, or items that are visual (use cards in a grid, e.g. MediaCard).
Server-side pagination over very large datasets: DataTable paginates client-side; pass one page of data and render Pagination yourself.

composition.role: Page container (mx-auto max-w-6xl, responsive padding, flex-col gap-6)

children.role: title + description; actions slot holds the primary Button (variant cta)
Toolbar (role=search): stacks on mobile, row from sm
Sortable, paginated rows; Badge in cells for status

layout: One primary action, in PageHeader actions. Row actions go in a trailing column (Menu or ghost Buttons).
Keep filter state in the page (or URL search params) and pass filtered rows to DataTable.
DataTable paginates internally (pageSize, default 10). Use the separate Pagination component only for server-side paging.
responsive: Toolbar: flex-col below sm, flex-row from sm; SearchInput grows (sm:flex-1), filters get fixed widths.
Wrap DataTable in overflow-x-auto so wide tables scroll inside the page instead of the page scrolling sideways.
Keep columns to what fits; drop secondary columns from the columns array on small screens rather than squeezing them.
accessibility: SearchInput and Select need aria-label when no visible <Label> is rendered.
Wrap the toolbar in role=search.
Communicate status with Badge text, not color alone.
Set emptyMessage to explain an empty filter result.
patterns.states: Loading: render ListSkeleton from page-states in place of the table. Error: ErrorState variant=error with Retry. No records at all (not just no matches): ErrorState variant=empty with the create action.
antiPatterns: Rebuilding sorting/pagination by hand around Table when DataTable already does it.
Filtering inside cell renderers instead of before passing data.
Importing ColumnDef from @tanstack/react-table without installing it: type columns as DataTableProps<Row, unknown>["columns"] or add the dependency.

patterns.name: Loading, empty and error states
patterns.summary: One AsyncContent wrapper that renders a skeleton, a recoverable error, an empty state with an action, or the content.
patterns.description: Every page or card that loads data needs all four states. Skeleton mirrors the content's shape while loading; ErrorState covers both failures (variant=error, with Retry) and empty collections (variant=empty, with the create action).
whenToUse: Any view backed by async data.
whenNotToUse: Inline field validation (use Input invalid + Alert in forms).
Transient success/failure notices after an action (use Toast).

composition.role: App-level helper (in the example) switching on a LoadState union

children.role: error: variant=error, role=alert, Retry Button in actions
empty: variant=empty, primary create Button in actions

layout: Render states in the same box the content will occupy, so the page does not jump.
Distinguish "no records yet" (empty state + create action) from "no matches" (DataTable emptyMessage + clear filters).
responsive: ErrorState is centered and width-agnostic; Skeleton rows should use the same responsive grid as the content.
accessibility: Loading container: role=status aria-live=polite with a visually hidden "Loading…".
Error container: role=alert so the failure is announced.
Retry is a real Button that re-runs the request; keep the user's filters and input.
antiPatterns: A full-page spinner for a partial reload.
Blank screens when a list is empty.
Error text with no recovery action.

patterns.name: Settings and profile page
patterns.summary: Tabbed settings with card sections: a profile form that saves explicitly and toggle rows that apply instantly.
patterns.description: Account, profile, notification and workspace preferences. Tabs group sections; each section is a card. Text fields are a form with a Save button and a success Alert; switches take effect immediately.
whenToUse: Users change preferences or profile fields.
whenNotToUse: Multi-step setup or onboarding (sequence the steps instead of tabs).
A single toggle (put it where it takes effect).
layout: SettingRow: text on the left, control on the right; one setting per row.
Forms save explicitly (submit Button bottom-right); switches apply immediately and need no Save.
responsive: SettingRow stacks (flex-col) below sm and becomes a row from sm.
With more than 4 tabs, consider orientation="vertical" Tabs on lg or separate routes.
accessibility: CardTitle renders an <h3>. Directly under the page's <h1> (PageHeader) pass aria-level={2} so the heading order does not skip a level.
Every Input/Select has a <Label htmlFor>. Mark required fields with Label required.
Switch is a button: connect it to its visible text with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby (or give it aria-label).
Show validation with Input invalid plus a text hint linked through aria-describedby.
Confirm saves with Alert variant=success; announce errors with Alert variant=destructive.
patterns.states: Disable Save while the form is invalid or submitting; keep user input after a failed save and show a destructive Alert.
antiPatterns: A Save button for switches that already applied.
Placeholder text used as the only label.
Using the deprecated Alert severity prop: use variant.
